title.$t: various artists - Intended Play 2005: Wrongs Of Spring

summary.$t: It's pretty much the direct opposite of spring here in the PNW. But, as I often say, there's never a bad time for a spring sampler, and Matador's 2005 entry in their long-running Intended Play series fits the bill. It leads off with one of my all-time favorite Interpol cuts, contributes a Yo La Tengo demo, and samples Mission Of Burma's digital-only, post-reunion live record, "Snapshot". Dead

summary.$t: It was a great week last week for crate digging. Things kicked off after a rare work-from-the-office day when I stopped by one of my regular haunts before coming home. I had seen a picture of their Monday night restock, showing two bookshelves full of CDs and cassettes. I knew there was quality to be found; I was proven correct when I walked out with 25 CDs at $2 a piece. Yesterday, I stopped in

As mid-90s rock radio promos go, this one is pretty good. It's hard to beat a lineup that leads off with Foo Fighters/Ben Folds 5/Buffalo Tom/Edwyn Collins. Add in some British indie from Teenage Fanclub, the Verve, and Sleeper, a pair of covers by Circle Jerks and Tricky, and a contribution by the tragically-underheard China Drum, and I'm left thinking, "I'd listen to this radio station RIGHT
